system.name: PUSHtap
system.one_liner: a PIM-based in-memory HTAP system that unifies OLTP row access and OLAP column access via interleaved CPU/PIM data placement

components.name: OLTP Engine
components.role: processes row-wise transactions on the database

components.name: OLAP Engine

components.name: PIM0

content.key_idea: OLTP/OLAP engines naturally access rows/columns respectively, and this mirrors the two physical access dimensions of DRAM-based PIM: CPU interleaving (ADE) and localized PIM access (IDE).
content.reading_order: Left panel (a) top-down: OLTP Engine, Database table, OLAP Engine; right panel (b) top-down: CPU, DRAM Bank grid with device columns, PIM units below.

summary: This figure motivates PUSHtap, a PIM-based in-memory HTAP database, by drawing a parallel between software workload access patterns and hardware memory access dimensions. Panel (a) shows a generic HTAP system where an OLTP engine reads/writes rows (e.g. R0) and an OLAP engine scans columns (e.g. C0) of a shared Database table. Panel (b) shows the corresponding DRAM-based PIM hardware: the CPU accesses data by interleaving across memory devices D0-D3 (the ADE dimension), while each PIM unit (PIM0-PIM3) accesses data locally within its own device (the IDE dimension). The two panels are drawn as simple boxes and a labeled grid table in a flat, pastel blue/green palette typical of a PowerPoint/Visio diagram, with green highlights picking out the example row and column. The figure sets up the paper's key insight that row-store maps naturally to CPU/ADE access and column-store to PIM/IDE access.
summary_zh: 该图展示 PUSHtap 的动机：(a) HTAP 系统中 OLTP 引擎按行访问、OLAP 引擎按列访问数据库；(b) 对应地，基于 DRAM 的 PIM 架构中 CPU 沿 ADE 维度跨设备交织访问，而 PIM 单元沿 IDE 维度在本地设备内访问，软硬件两个维度形成类比。
